title: Materiality and the risk response — Tallis Foods
instructions: You are setting materiality and planning responses for the audit of **Tallis Foods**, a stable, profitable private company. Firm policy: overall materiality = 5% of pretax income from continuing operations; performance materiality = 75% of overall; clearly trivial = 5% of overall.

exhibits.title: Data
exhibits.content:
- Pretax income from continuing operations: **$3,200,000**
- Planned audit risk for inventory existence: 5%
- Assessed inherent risk: 100%; assessed control risk: 20% (controls tested and effective)

exhibits.title: Risk assessments
exhibits.content:
| Assertion | Inherent risk | Control risk |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue cut-off | High | High (no reliance) |
| Prepaid insurance existence | Low | Maximum (not tested) |
| Inventory existence | High | Low (tested) |

parts.prompt: Compute the thresholds and detection risk.

rows.label: Acceptable detection risk for inventory existence (%)

parts.prompt: Select the most appropriate substantive approach for each assertion.

rows.label: Revenue cut-off
rows.answer: Extensive tests of details at year-end with larger samples
rows.explanation: High RMM → low acceptable detection risk → the most persuasive evidence at year-end.

rows.label: Prepaid insurance existence
rows.explanation: Low inherent risk and a small balance allow less extensive procedures — but some substantive work is still required for material items.

rows.label: Inventory existence
rows.answer: Moderate testing, possibly at an interim date
rows.explanation: Effective controls reduce RMM, permitting some reduction in the extent of testing.

rows.explanation: Above clearly trivial; accumulate even though it is below materiality.
